# dsh-prompt-recall

**Take the last prompt back.** One icon sits under the newest prompt you sent — in
the same row as *

copy*, and drawn by the shipped action-button style. Clicking it
stops the running turn, rewinds the

conversation to just before that prompt, and
puts its text back in the message box to edit and send

sation to just before that prompt, and
puts its text back in the message box to edit and send again.
**English** | 简体中文
## What it contributes
| Surface | What it does |
| the newest prompt's action row | adds one icon button beside the shipped *copy* button, styled by

that button's own class |
| Locale namespace `dsh-prompt-recall` | English and Simplified Chinese co

py for the tooltip, the busy state, and the three failure notices |
| `conversation.input.right` | h
osts the controller that owns the button and drains a recalled draft into the composer — it renders
no visible control of its own |

No host route, no host service, no Config. The host half (`exports["."]`) exists
only so the Loader
row can carry the browser half (`exports["./client"]`).
## What one click does
[代码示例省略，未执行]

1. **Stop.** The in-flight turn is cancelled on its own session scope, exactly as
the composer's Sto

p button does it. A rejection here is swallowed — an idle
session has nothing to cancel, and that mu

st not block the rewind.
2. **Rewind.** The conversation continues from an exact prefix of its own l

og.
3. **Restore.** The recalled text is staged for the child session's composer and
applied as it m

ounts, then the caret is returned to it.
4. **Retire.** The session the gesture came from moves to t

he archive set, so the
conversation exists once — the sidebar shows where you are, not everywhere yo

u
have been. This runs **last**, after the navigation: archiving the session on
screen clears the ma

in panel, so doing it first would blank the view before the
child opens.
## Why the conversation continues in a new session

A Session log is an append-only durable record, and a live Agent holds it open.
There is no "delete

the last turn" operation, and rewriting the log under a running
Agent would corrupt the session. The

platform's own answer to *continue from an
earlier point* is `session/fork` — copy an exact event p

refix into a new Session —
which is precisely what the shipped **branch** action does.
Recall is that same operation, cut at a different boundary:
| | cut at | you get |
| branch (shipped) | the end of the turn you forked from | a copy of everything, to try a different

continuation |
| recall (this plugin) | just before the prompt was queued | a continuation whose his
tory does not contain that prompt |

The child keeps the working directory, the agent preset and the workspace, and its
title increments,
so the sidebar never shows two indistinguishable rows.

Recall is repeatable: every recall cuts one prompt further back and retires the
session it came from

, so a rewind chain always presents exactly one visible
conversation.
## What happens to the old session: archive, not delete

A fork on its own would leave the conversation standing twice. So recall retires
the session it came

from — and the operation DSH offers for that is **archive**.
There is no session delete anywhere in

the platform (`archiveSession` /
`unarchiveSession` are the whole vocabulary; the `_deleteSession`

in the session
index is search-cache maintenance, and `workspaces.delete` removes a *workspace*).
Th
at suits this gesture:

- **the log is untouched** — the withdrawn prompt is still inside the retired
session, so nothing is

awal** — the durable archive set is what a provider's
`agent/pre-step` wake gate reads, so a retired

tate the shipped ⌘⇧A shortcut writes**, with
`stopActivity` — the escalation DSH's own confirmation

offers when a session has
work in flight, which recall has already decided for you.

**Getting one back:** the sidebar's view options filter sessions by archived
state (`default` / `sho

w` / `only`), and a session search result for an archived
session carries an unarchive button. No fi
le editing, no restart.

If retiring fails — a session the registry does not know yet is the usual cause —
the recall keeps e

verything it already did and says so in the new conversation
("the previous session could not be arc

hived — it is still in the sidebar")
rather than throwing the gesture away.

Recall is **not offered inside a subagent session**: its transcript is its
parent's evidence rather

than a conversation, so forking it would mint an ordinary
session out of a subagent prefix, and reti

ring it would remove it from its
parent's catalog.
## Where the button is placed, and why it is placed by DOM

The Chat view exposes no slot for a *user* message's action row.
`conversation.chat.assistant-action

s` and `conversation.chat.turnTail` both render
for a **completed** turn, so neither exists while th

e Agent is still working —
which is exactly when a recall button has to be reachable. Shadowing the

ll working —
which is exactly when a recall button has to be reachable. Shadowing the whole
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

- **Recall is not undo of the model's work.** A turn that already ran tools leaves
those effects beh

ind; the rewind removes the prompt from the conversation, not
what the filesystem did in the meantim

e.
- **The child session is a real session.** It appears in the sidebar and counts
against the sessi

on list, exactly like a branch does.
- **The retired session is archived, not deleted** — it stays o

n disk, leaves the
default sidebar list, and comes back with unarchive. If you would rather keep
the

pre-recall session visible, unarchive it after the gesture; there is no
session delete in DSH to of

fer instead.
- **The placement contract is DSH's DOM.** If a future Harness renames
`data-chat-flow-

kind`, `data-clock` or the action-button class, the button
disappears (it fails soft — no crash, no

broken row). The three selectors are
declared in one place, `anchor.ts`, with its tests.
- **Attachm
ents are not restored** — see the table above.
